_description: Task13 WEIGHTING field (unit probe), COARSE transcription -- the 0.22mm far-field grid for the 5x5 LArPix v2a tile at the true 4.4mm pitch. The fine sibling (example_gen_pixel_with_grid_task13_fine.json) carries the true design values unsnapped. SNAPPED PAD/GAP, AND WHY ONLY HERE: the design values are pixelSize 3.5, pixelGap 0.9, chamfer_r 0.7. gcd(35,9) = 1, so NO spacing coarser than 0.1mm divides both the pad and the gap exactly and some snapping on the coarse grid is unavoidable. 0.22mm was chosen because it snaps the pad to 3.52mm, only +1.1% in area, against +5.8% for 0.2 or 0.4. That error matters more than it looks: the far field in the final stitched output IS the upsampled coarse solution, so a coarse pad-area error biases the far weighting field by about the same percentage, and it is a SMOOTH error that the Laplacian residual metric cannot detect. The design values are preserved as the _design_* keys below; the generators ignore _design_* keys. CELL COUNTS AT 0.22mm: pixelSize 3.52 -> 16 cells, pixelGap 0.88 -> 4 cells, chamfer_r 0.66 -> 3 cells (0.7/0.22 = 3.18). PAD PLANE 9.9 IS EXACT ON BOTH GRIDS: 9.9/0.22 = 45.0 and 9.9/0.1 = 99.0 with no floating-point shortfall, so the bare int() at gen_pcb_drift_pixel_with_grid.py:474 is safe on either. That exactness is what chose 0.22mm over 0.44mm, which would force the pad plane onto a multiple of 2.2mm (8.8 or 11.0). The value was 10.0 until Phase 0/Step 5; that produced the SAME plane, since int(10.0/0.22) is also 45, but it read as a geometry the file did not have. LAMINATE THINNED TO 0.22mm (Phase 0/Step 6): padThickness and FR4Thickness are 0.22mm on this grid, against the fine grid's 0.05/0.1mm, so that both round to ONE cell here (n_pad + n_fr4 - 1 = 1) and the pad top lands at (45+1)*0.22 = 10.12mm instead of the 10.56mm that 0.4mm layers gave by rounding to 2 cells each. The drift pair must agree with the weighting pair about where the pad surface is, so the two coarse files carry the same laminate. PITCH MUST STAY EXACTLY 4.4mm = 20 coarse cells: 16 + 4 = 20. hybrid_iterate.py _cells() requires the transverse extent to be a WHOLE number of cells and raises otherwise, so this is a hard constraint, not a preference; the two coarse files must also stay consistent with each other, since the drift tile and the weighting probe have to model the SAME pad. NO GridPotential and NO CathodePotential, deliberately: the weighting potential is a dimensionless unit probe in [0,1], not volts -- collecting pixel = 1 and every other electrode including the cathode = 0 -- so the cathode formula in the drift configs (example_gen_pcb_drift_pixel_task13_*.json) does not apply here. DEPTH: driftZDepth 79.15 with pixelPlaneLowEdgePosition 9.9 tracks the drift pair's 69.25mm geometry; the weighting solve itself does not use a drift length, but the number is kept in step so the file handed to induce-pixel is not stale. It is deliberately NOT rounded to 79.2: the domain closes at ceil(79.15/0.22) = 360 coarse cells = 79.2mm, the last plane of the 361-node coarse z grid, so there is no dead space above the cathode, while the launch node 79.15 does not land on that grounded plane. gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py grounds its cathode at int(round(driftZDepth/spacing)) = 360, the same plane. SHIELD GRID OFF (GridHoleShape 'None', Phase 0/Step 8): inherited from the older with-grid task13 work and never intended for this WOGRID LArPix v2a geometry; the drift pair was cleared in Step 7 and these two must match it, since the drift field and the weighting probe have to model the same geometry. This was NOT inert while it was on: gen_pcb_pixel_with_grid.py:296 called draw_3Dstrips_sq, which writes into barr only, so the strips became a GROUNDED perforated electrode -- for a weighting field that is a Ramo non-collecting electrode held at W=0, shielding the pad. Verified on the coarse grid: the old grid plane (index 52 at 11.44mm) held 4400 cells and now holds none; the occupied planes are the pad block (44/45/46, 6400 cells each), the z=0 face and the cathode at 360. Transverse edges stay fix,fix,fix on the 22.0mm (5 x 4.4mm) domain. Effect on the far tail is large: coarse W on the pad-centre axis is 6.4x larger at z=25mm, 8.1x at 40mm and 10.5x at 60mm with the grid gone, because the grounded strips had been shielding it. NOTE the 'None' branch works by FALL-THROUGH -- there is no else on the circular/square test -- so any typo, 'squrae' for instance, also silently means no grid. PROBE: Npixels 5 at the 4.4mm pitch = 22.0mm transverse, i.e. 100 cells at this file's 0.22mm spacing, solved NON-periodic (edges fix,fix,fix) so phi_w decays to ~0 at the tile edges instead of wrapping; a weighting field cannot be solved on the single periodic pixel tile the drift field uses.
